question: How does a skill fundamentally differ from CLAUDE.md?

options.text: A skill can use only one tool
options.explanation: A skill can use any number of tools specified in allowed-tools

options.text: A skill is written in JavaScript, while CLAUDE.md is in Markdown
options.explanation: Both files use Markdown. A skill (SKILL.md) additionally has YAML frontmatter for metadata

options.text: A skill runs faster than CLAUDE.md
options.explanation: Speed does not depend on the instruction format. The difference is when the instruction loads into context

options.text: A skill loads into context only on request, while CLAUDE.md is always loaded
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md is an always-on instruction that Claude reads on every launch. A skill is an on-demand instruction, loaded only when needed. This saves context

question: Which frontmatter field is critical for automatic skill selection?

options.text: allowed-tools
options.explanation: allowed-tools restricts the tool set, but does not affect automatic skill selection

options.text: name
options.explanation: name defines the slash command name, but Claude uses description to match the skill to the user's task

options.text: description
options.explanation: Claude matches the user's request against skill descriptions. Without this field, the skill is available only via direct /skill-name invocation

options.text: model
options.explanation: model overrides the model used, but does not participate in skill selection

question: What does the context: fork field in skill frontmatter do?

options.text: Runs the skill in an isolated context, separate from the main dialog
options.explanation: context: fork means the skill doesn't see the dialog history and doesn't clutter it with its output -- like opening a task in a separate tab

options.text: Runs the skill in parallel with the main process
options.explanation: fork is not about parallel execution, but about context isolation -- the skill works from a clean slate

options.text: Copies the skill to another directory before running
options.explanation: fork relates to the conversation (dialog) context, not the filesystem

options.text: Creates a git branch for the skill's work
options.explanation: fork in the context of skills is not related to git. This is dialog context isolation, not code branching

question: The user invoked /deploy staging v2.1.0. What value will the $ARGUMENTS variable have?

options.text: staging v2.1.0
options.explanation: $ARGUMENTS contains all arguments as-is, without the command name: staging v2.1.0

options.text: /deploy staging v2.1.0
options.explanation: $ARGUMENTS does not include the slash and command name -- only the arguments after the name

options.text: staging
options.explanation: This is the value of $1 (first argument). $ARGUMENTS contains all arguments: staging v2.1.0

options.text: deploy staging v2.1.0
options.explanation: $ARGUMENTS contains only the arguments, without the command name. The command name is available via $0

question: Where should skills that need to be available to the whole project team be placed?

options.text: ~/.claude/skills/
options.explanation: This is the personal skills directory in the user's home folder -- it is not committed to git and not visible to the team

options.text: .claude/skills/
options.explanation: Team skills are placed in .claude/skills/ inside the repository -- they are committed to git and available to all project participants

options.text: In the repository root next to package.json
options.explanation: Claude Code looks for skills in specific directories (.claude/skills/, ~/.claude/skills/), not arbitrary locations

options.text: plugins/skills/
options.explanation: This directory is for skills from connected plugins, not for project team skills

question: What are supporting files in the context of skills?

options.text: Additional files next to SKILL.md: templates, examples, references
options.explanation: Next to SKILL.md you can place any supporting files -- Claude gets access to them via ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}

options.text: Backup copies of SKILL.md in case of corruption
options.explanation: Supporting files are working files, not backups

options.text: Dependency files that the skill installs via npm
options.explanation: Supporting files are not npm dependencies, but auxiliary files (templates, examples, references) next to SKILL.md

options.text: Skill execution logs
options.explanation: Supporting files are created by the developer in advance, not generated during skill execution

question: Which built-in skill runs a prompt on multiple files?

options.text: /loop
options.explanation: /loop runs a command repeating over time (every N minutes), not across a file list

options.text: /glob
options.explanation: glob is a file search tool, not a built-in skill for batch processing

options.text: /batch
options.explanation: /batch takes a prompt and a file pattern, then applies the prompt to each found file

options.text: /simplify
options.explanation: /simplify analyzes code for quality and reusability, but doesn't do batch file processing

question: Why is it bad to create one 500-line skill that does everything: deployment, migrations, tests, and monitoring?

options.text: Claude Code forbids SKILL.md longer than 100 lines
options.explanation: There's no technical limit on SKILL.md size -- the problem is efficiency and maintainability

options.text: Vague description degrades automatic selection
options.explanation: A description like 'All DevOps operations' is too general -- Claude won't be able to accurately determine when to suggest the skill

options.text: Claude spends more tokens parsing the huge instruction
options.explanation: The entire SKILL.md text loads into context -- 500 lines on every invocation, even if only the deployment part is needed

options.text: Impossible to set different allowed-tools for different operations
options.explanation: allowed-tools is set at the skill level. One skill = one permission set. Deployment needs kubectl, tests need npm test

options.text: The skill works without sending data to the Anthropic API
options.explanation: A skill is an instruction for Claude, which is always processed via the API. The field controls invocation method, not data routing

options.text: Switches the skill to use a local model
options.explanation: Claude Code does not support switching to local models via skill frontmatter

options.text: Forbids the skill from using the AI model
options.explanation: A skill is an instruction for an AI model, without which it makes no sense. The field forbids automatic invocation, not model usage

options.text: The skill can only be invoked via slash command, Claude won't suggest it automatically
options.explanation: For dangerous skills (deployment, migrations) this is important: they should not run accidentally via auto-selection

question: What is the ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} variable used for inside SKILL.md?

options.text: Path to the project root
options.explanation: Project root is accessible other ways. ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} is the path to the directory containing SKILL.md

options.text: Path to the skill's directory -- for accessing supporting files
options.explanation: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} points to the directory containing SKILL.md. Use it to refer to templates, examples, and references next to the skill

options.text: Path to the global directory of all skills
options.explanation: The variable points to a specific skill, not the directory of all skills

options.text: Path to the user's home directory
options.explanation: Home directory is ~/ or $HOME. ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} points to the specific skill's directory

question: A skill is defined with paths: ["src/**/*.test.ts"]. When does it activate?

options.text: When Claude works with files matching the *.test.ts pattern
options.explanation: paths is conditional activation: the skill connects automatically when Claude reads or edits files matching the specified glob pattern

options.text: Always, if the project has test files
options.explanation: paths activates the skill when working with specific files in the current session, not simply by their presence in the project

options.text: On every Claude Code launch in the src/ directory
options.explanation: Activation is tied to working with specific files matching the pattern, not the current working directory

options.text: Only on direct slash-command invocation
options.explanation: paths provides automatic activation without the need for manual invocation

question: You're creating a code review skill. Which allowed-tools set is correct?

options.text: Don't specify allowed-tools at all
options.explanation: Without an explicit limit, the skill inherits all session permissions -- better to explicitly specify the minimum needed

options.text: allowed-tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash(git diff:*), Bash(git log:*)
options.explanation: Code review requires reading files and git history. No Write, Edit, or arbitrary Bash commands needed -- principle of least privilege

options.text: allowed-tools: "*"
options.explanation: Code review doesn't need Write, Bash(rm*) or WebFetch access -- why give excessive permissions?

options.text: allowed-tools: Bash(*)
options.explanation: Review doesn't need arbitrary Bash commands -- git diff and git log are sufficient for change analysis

options.text: The skill is available only to administrators
options.explanation: Claude Code has no role/admin system. user-invocable determines whether a human can invoke the skill via /

options.text: The skill works only in CI/CD, not in interactive mode
options.explanation: user-invocable is not related to CI/CD. This is a restriction on manual invocation via slash command

options.text: Hides the skill from the slash command list -- it's available only to Claude
options.explanation: A skill with user-invocable: false is not displayed to the user. It's intended for internal use -- for example, as an auxiliary skill invoked from another skill

options.text: Forbids the user from seeing the skill's results
options.explanation: Skill results are visible to the user. The field controls manual invocation ability, not result visibility

question: How should you correctly refer to supporting files inside SKILL.md?

options.text: Via import: import config from 'templates/config.yaml'
options.explanation: SKILL.md is Markdown with instructions for Claude, not a JavaScript module. Imports don't work here

options.text: Via relative path: ./templates/config.yaml
options.explanation: Relative path depends on the current working directory, which can be anything. ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} always points to the skill directory

options.text: Via absolute path: /home/user/.claude/skills/deploy/templates/config.yaml
options.explanation: Absolute paths are tied to a specific machine -- colleagues will have a different path. Use ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}

options.text: Via variable: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/templates/config.yaml
options.explanation: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} reliably points to the skill directory regardless of working directory or machine
